release_summary.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix 'whatever is causing the wrong bills' (CL-01), after dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month between Jul and Aug-Sep 2026 (E-07). Investigation established that the surge is not a response-speed problem (SLA still met, E-03) and not a tariff change (E-02, E-04), but is driven, for the ESTIMATED-read portion of disputed bills (1240/3025, E-01), by billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12) rejecting valid, timely AMI reads as 'high consumption' because it compares raw register values against m3 history without unit conversion, while firmware v4.2 meters report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13); this mechanism accounts for 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (95.5%, E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16). The mechanism behind the larger ACTUAL-read cohort (1785/3025, 59%, E-01) remains unestablished. The release delivers diagnostic re-confirmation of the BV-17/firmware mechanism (diagnose_billing_defect against DA-MDMS and DA-RULES) plus ongoing dispute-volume and response-SLA monitoring (DA-TICKET), with no automated bill writes (per constraint K-BILLWRITE) and no automated ticket-response sending. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE Gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, with two verification obligations (VOB-R-2 on send authority, VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM on the ACTUAL-read cohort) still open but outside the committed release scope, and because the structural BV-17 patch itself is not feasible within contest time.
key_points: Requester's framing (auto-answer tickets + auto-fix the cause, CL-01) was tested as a hypothesis (H-CS-RESPONSE-FRAMING) and rejected: dispute response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, E-03), so the surge is not a response-capacity issue.

Root cause for the ESTIMATED-read disputed cohort is confirmed: billing rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), rejects valid AMI reads as high-consumption because it compares unconverted raw register values to m3 history while firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13); this explains 1184/1240 (95.5%) of ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16).

Earlier hypotheses were ruled out for this cohort: tariff changes (E-02, E-04), field staffing/route-completion shortfall (E-05, E-06), and AMI delivery failure (E-01, E-11, E-16) do not explain the dominant mechanism, even though a real 7-point route-completion gap (0.88 vs 0.95 target) exists (E-05).
The mechanism behind the ACTUAL-read cohort (59% of disputed bills, 1785/3025, E-01) is unresolved and tracked as unknown U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM / VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.

Release scope delivered: re-confirmation of the BV-17/firmware-v4.2 defect via diagnose_billing_defect against DA-MDMS and DA-RULES, plus ongoing monitor_dispute_volume and monitor_response_sla against DA-TICKET (solution design SD-2).

No automated bill corrections are made; billing adjustments remain a manual Billing Operations action, consistent with constraint K-BILLWRITE requiring Billing Operations authority for any bill write.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE Gate result was only CONDITIONAL_PASS, with VOB-R-2 (send authority for drafted ticket responses) and VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM both open but classified as outside the committed release scope.
limitations_explained: The actual structural fix — patching rule BV-17 to convert firmware v4.2 raw register values (0.1 m3) to m3 before comparison — was not done; it is flagged as not feasible within contest time, so the rejections and resulting disputes keep accruing until an external patch is applied.
The ACTUAL-read cohort, 59% of all disputed bills, cannot be addressed or even explained in this release because VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM is open and its underlying mechanism is unknown.
No analysis or drafting of dispute ticket responses was performed this release because VOB-R-2 (whether the agent has authority to auto-send responses without per-response human review) is open.

Manual-read route completion remains below target (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-05) and is treated as a secondary, unaddressed gap, since it was ruled out as the primary driver of the confirmed ESTIMATED-read mechanism.

The diagnose_billing_defect work against DA-RULES/DA-MDMS in this release mainly re-confirms the already-established ESTIMATED-cohort mechanism rather than producing new findings; its ongoing value is limited to detecting future rule or firmware changes.
The DEFINE Gate for this problem definition only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some verification items were deferred as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before release.

causal_chain: Firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report raw register readings in '0.1 m3' units instead of 'm3' (E-13).
Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, flags high consumption by comparing the raw register value directly to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none (E-12).

For v4.2 meters this raw value is effectively 10x the true m3 reading, so BV-17 rejects valid, timely AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION even though the read was delivered before cutoff (E-11, E-13).
1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills show exactly this pattern: ami_read_before_cutoff=true, billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, firmware=v4.2 (E-11).
Rejected reads force estimate substitution in the meter-to-cash process instead of billing from the valid AMI read (P-M2C step: estimate substitution when no accepted read).

Customers receiving estimate-substituted/incorrect bills file disputes, and ticket volume roughly doubles from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026), aligning with BV-17's 2026-08-01 deployment date (E-07, E-12).

output.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix 'whatever is causing the wrong bills' (CL-01), after dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month between Jul and Aug-Sep 2026 (E-07). Investigation established that the surge is not a response-speed problem (SLA still met, E-03) and not a tariff change (E-02, E-04), but is driven, for the ESTIMATED-read portion of disputed bills (1240/3025, E-01), by billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12) rejecting valid, timely AMI reads as 'high consumption' because it compares raw register values against m3 history without unit conversion, while firmware v4.2 meters report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13); this mechanism accounts for 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (95.5%, E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16). The mechanism behind the larger ACTUAL-read cohort (1785/3025, 59%, E-01) remains unestablished. The release delivers diagnostic re-confirmation of the BV-17/firmware mechanism (diagnose_billing_defect against DA-MDMS and DA-RULES) plus ongoing dispute-volume and response-SLA monitoring (DA-TICKET), with no automated bill writes (per constraint K-BILLWRITE) and no automated ticket-response sending. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE Gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, with two verification obligations (VOB-R-2 on send authority, VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM on the ACTUAL-read cohort) still open but outside the committed release scope, and because the structural BV-17 patch itself is not feasible within contest time.
key_points: Requester's framing (auto-answer tickets + auto-fix the cause, CL-01) was tested as a hypothesis (H-CS-RESPONSE-FRAMING) and rejected: dispute response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, E-03), so the surge is not a response-capacity issue.

Root cause for the ESTIMATED-read disputed cohort is confirmed: billing rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), rejects valid AMI reads as high-consumption because it compares unconverted raw register values to m3 history while firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13); this explains 1184/1240 (95.5%) of ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-11, E-14, E-15, E-16).

Earlier hypotheses were ruled out for this cohort: tariff changes (E-02, E-04), field staffing/route-completion shortfall (E-05, E-06), and AMI delivery failure (E-01, E-11, E-16) do not explain the dominant mechanism, even though a real 7-point route-completion gap (0.88 vs 0.95 target) exists (E-05).
The mechanism behind the ACTUAL-read cohort (59% of disputed bills, 1785/3025, E-01) is unresolved and tracked as unknown U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM / VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.

Release scope delivered: re-confirmation of the BV-17/firmware-v4.2 defect via diagnose_billing_defect against DA-MDMS and DA-RULES, plus ongoing monitor_dispute_volume and monitor_response_sla against DA-TICKET (solution design SD-2).

No automated bill corrections are made; billing adjustments remain a manual Billing Operations action, consistent with constraint K-BILLWRITE requiring Billing Operations authority for any bill write.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE Gate result was only CONDITIONAL_PASS, with VOB-R-2 (send authority for drafted ticket responses) and VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM both open but classified as outside the committed release scope.
limitations_explained: The actual structural fix — patching rule BV-17 to convert firmware v4.2 raw register values (0.1 m3) to m3 before comparison — was not done; it is flagged as not feasible within contest time, so the rejections and resulting disputes keep accruing until an external patch is applied.
The ACTUAL-read cohort, 59% of all disputed bills, cannot be addressed or even explained in this release because VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM is open and its underlying mechanism is unknown.
No analysis or drafting of dispute ticket responses was performed this release because VOB-R-2 (whether the agent has authority to auto-send responses without per-response human review) is open.

Manual-read route completion remains below target (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-05) and is treated as a secondary, unaddressed gap, since it was ruled out as the primary driver of the confirmed ESTIMATED-read mechanism.

The diagnose_billing_defect work against DA-RULES/DA-MDMS in this release mainly re-confirms the already-established ESTIMATED-cohort mechanism rather than producing new findings; its ongoing value is limited to detecting future rule or firmware changes.
The DEFINE Gate for this problem definition only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some verification items were deferred as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before release.
